scope: Research catalog behind the SportsDesk security/fraud detectors and model. Every threshold below is measured from this repo at the cited module:line; nothing here is invented. External prior art is listed separately and is terminology-only, not a threshold source.

terminology.definition: Placing a bet while physically or electronically closer to live action than the operator's feed, so the bet is placed after the outcome is effectively known.
An account whose wager lands within seconds of its session starting or of the previous wager — the pattern of a scripted or feed-assisted executor rather than a browsing customer.
Two or more logins on the same /24 (or IPv6 /64) that place fast wagers within a minute of each other on the same skin — separate identities driven from one location.
A cluster of accounts whose traffic originates from a hosting/provider address range rather than a residential carrier, indicating automated account farming.
A session that spends a long time viewing prices without wagering, or an account that repeatedly places only after a price has moved in its favour.
An account used to conceal the identity or volume of the real bettor, often sharing an office IP with other logins while appearing independent.
A high-value account whose steady losses subsidise a linked cluster; enforcement that closes the cluster must not also lose the donor's revenue.
A pattern where an account shows a small or losing baseline and then a sudden large step-up with strong ROI — the profile the desk's GATE-SURV-02 treats as fraud-suspected.
Wins that settle inside the confirmation delay window (or immediately after a pre-bet score), which is only possible if the operator's confirmation control failed.
A wager placed after the relevant score already guarantees the selection wins — a placement control failure or courtsiding signal.
A fast, coordinated price move immediately before a score; a bet placed within 15s (or 5s) of a score is the desk's steam-adjacent window.
One person operating multiple identities to multiply limits, bonuses or exposure. Detected through shared infrastructure (IP, /24, /64) and coordinated timing.
A graded wager whose credit was reversed by hand or by the platform — a strong desk-side signal that something about the ticket or the account was disputed.
A wager whose lifecycle includes a manual operator action. Manual handling correlates with exceptions and disputed tickets.

priorArtRegister.basis: shared infrastructure and coordinated timing rather than identity documents
bet-to-event latency smaller than the operator's own feed and confirmation delay
session or placement behaviour consistent with scraping and accepting only stale prices
an account or office whose losses subsidise a flagged cluster; step-up asymmetry

priorArtRegister.pattern: data-integrity failure (a security finding in its own right)
priorArtRegister.basis: a detector computed on stale, missing or fixture data is worse than no detector

modelLimits: The model predicts a weak proxy label built from the desk's own flags (suspected-bot / reversed-credit / manual-log), not a confirmed fraud outcome.
The corpus is a single live GSLive export snapshot; it is not a longitudinal history of the same accounts.
The source corpus is ephemeral and untracked (Scratch/), so a missing corpus must be reported as missing, never as a zero-row or clean result.
Fixture-derived sources (the bundled customer book, hardcoded IP-tracker clusters) are excluded from fitting and appear only as labelled context.
There is no account↔login bridge between the GSLive report corpus (numeric userID) and the F402 ticker (string Login); cross-source account joins are not claimed.
IP addresses are masked; findings identify clusters by masked value + stable tag + /24 prefix, never by raw address.
The model has no enforcement power: findings are evidence for an operator decision, not an action against an account.
No detector in this plugin has been validated against confirmed fraud cases; their thresholds are the desk's own constants and are reported with provenance.
dataQualityRules: MISSING is a measured state, never zero.
A stale source is still shown, labelled stale with its age.
A fixture source carries provenance "fixture" and is never fitted.
An empty capture (e.g. getWebLog responseBytes 21) means rows are MISSING, not that zero events occurred.
A derived audit with a known argument defect (targetAccount "--help") is surfaced as SUSPECT_AUDIT_DEFECT rather than trusted.
priorArtNaming: courtsiding / courtside data-scouting; late-bet abuse / latency arbitrage / live time delay; multi-accounting / sybil accounts / promo (bonus) abuse / device farm / account takeover; match-fixing / spot-fixing / suspicious betting alert / steam move / line movement; chip dumping / soft play / collusion / whipsawing / value transfer / money mule; weak supervision / proxy label / PR-AUC / precision@k / model risk management / explainability. 'Donor' and 'donor shield' are this desk's jargon, not standard industry terms.

externalPriorArt.title: RTS 15 — In-play betting
externalPriorArt.claim: Live TV is delayed and customers must be told others may have more up-to-date information, so a bet-to-event latency below the operator's own delay is the structural courtsiding window.

externalPriorArt.title: RTS 11 — Limiting collusion and cheating
externalPriorArt.claim: Operators must deter, prevent and detect collusion/cheating, detect shared-table/address players and chip dumping, and keep investigation records (reason, outcome, evidence).

externalPriorArt.title: Reminder of identity verification requirements for remote operators
externalPriorArt.claim: Name/address/DOB must be verified before gambling; initials, nicknames, commercial addresses and fuzzy matches are insufficient.

externalPriorArt.title: Directive 2 of 2018 — Player Protection Directive
externalPriorArt.claim: Multiple accounts are contemplated but limits and self-exclusion must apply across them; operators must run analytical/behaviour-monitoring tools with designed or evolving parameters and retain investigation records.

externalPriorArt.title: Late Bet Score (LBS) API — FAQ
externalPriorArt.claim: A production per-account ML score (0.00-1.00) for late-bet abuse built on timing anomalies and value spikes; >=0.90 is strong likelihood and drives a dynamic live time delay or manual review.

externalPriorArt.title: Latency Indicator (beta)
externalPriorArt.claim: Each match carries an expected latency level (0-2s low .. 16s+ exceptional), updated live when delay crosses a threshold — the feed-side context needed to separate a fast bettor from a stalled feed.

externalPriorArt.title: Integrity in Action 2024
externalPriorArt.claim: 1,108 suspicious matches across 12 sports in 95 countries in 2024; AI became the primary monitoring tool for four sports; a 117-operator Integrity Exchange produced 291 suspicious-match identifications from operator data.

externalPriorArt.title: ITIA v Khudoiani & Movsisyan — decision
externalPriorArt.claim: Two chair umpires manipulated a handheld electronic scoring device to facilitate third-party betting — official-data manipulation produces the same bet-to-score timing signature as courtsiding.

externalPriorArt.title: ESIC integrity-in-esports presentation (Nevada Gaming Policy Committee)
externalPriorArt.claim: Integrity monitoring draws on supplier and bookmaker alerts (450 bookmakers referenced), an intelligence database and participant alerts.

externalPriorArt.title: In-play betting volume baseline and outlier detection (2605.30209)
externalPriorArt.claim: In-play is roughly 40% of volume with scarce verified fixing ground truth; the published approach models expected in-play volume from match state and flags deviations instead of claiming outcome labels.

externalPriorArt.title: Chip dumping guide
externalPriorArt.claim: Chip dumping transfers value to an accomplice through deliberate losing play; intent is hard to prove, so operators use linked identities, one-directional value and funding anomalies.

externalPriorArt.title: AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (AI 100-1)
externalPriorArt.claim: Explainability/interpretability are trustworthiness characteristics; training-data provenance supports transparency, audit and accountability.

externalPriorArt.title: SR 11-7 — Guidance on Model Risk Management
externalPriorArt.claim: Validation has three elements (conceptual soundness, ongoing monitoring, outcomes analysis) and documentation must let an unfamiliar party understand operation, limitations and key assumptions.

externalPriorArt.title: Snorkel: Fast Training Set Generation for Weak Supervision (1711.10160)
externalPriorArt.claim: Labelling functions written by experts can have unknown accuracies and correlations; a model trained on their denoised consensus is a model of the rules, not of adjudicated outcomes.

externalPriorArt.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
externalPriorArt.claim: On strongly imbalanced data ROC can be deceptive; precision-recall and precision@k describe the analyst queue honestly.

externalPriorArt.title: Account-behaviour predictors in a 1,470-customer sports/race betting study
externalPriorArt.claim: Behavioural account aggregates (age, deposits per active day, average stake, days since betting) were the most predictive variables with roughly 30 days of data.

externalPriorArt.title: Beating the bookies with their own numbers (1710.02824)
externalPriorArt.claim: Closing odds are the standard reference for whether a bet beat the market, and operator limiting is a confounder for later behaviour — CLV is a sharp-account feature, not a fraud label.

externalPriorArt.title: Graph-based fraud detection survey (1910.11299)
externalPriorArt.claim: Fraud can appear as a distinctive edge, node or subgraph (e.g. money-laundering groups), so shared-infrastructure graphs are evidence in their own right.

externalPriorArt.title: iGaming registration fraud detection
externalPriorArt.claim: Detection stacks device fingerprinting, identity enrichment, IP intelligence and behavioural signals; data-centre/VPN classes are supporting evidence, never a single conclusive flag.

externalPriorArt.title: Promo abuse
externalPriorArt.claim: Promo abusers reset devices, spoof location and script the same play across hundreds of accounts; detection pairs location, device and behaviour as network graphs.

externalPriorArt.title: Managed Trading Services (MTS)
externalPriorArt.claim: Trading systems are explicitly risk and liability management services — the desk's own liability limits belong in the same control plane as the fraud findings.

externalPriorArt.title: Transaction 3.0 — rejected liability limit
externalPriorArt.claim: Tickets can be rejected with a liability-limit error; acceptance/rejection behaviour is itself a measurable signal.

externalPriorArt.title: Global Monitoring & Alert Platform
externalPriorArt.claim: Industry monitoring is a distinct function with its own alert platform across operators.

proposedDetectors.rationale: Per bet, compute t_accept - t_last_score and t_place - t_last_score for the same event/period; flag accounts clustering in the final seconds before a score change, normalised by the match latency level.
Join feed-latency level/change events to bet arrivals; flag a burst accepted while the feed is stalled or just after a stall.
Compare accept-delay with the account's effective live delay and the house default; flag sub-delay acceptances.
Transparent daily per-account score (0-100) over late-bet rate, median accept-to-score gap, odds drift at accept and stake spike, published with contributions and cutoffs.
Flag manual overrides and their effect: post-override accept latency, odds change and settlement time.
Account nodes from ipAddress, /24 and /64 prefixes, masked clusters with account/agent counts and cross-agent links.
New accounts and first bets per device/IP-subnet/payment instrument per hour; flag >k with a minimum cluster size and at least two independent signals.
Flag bonus claims or withdrawals before full verification, name/DOB mismatch and a payment instrument shared across accounts; insufficientData when KYC/payment fields are absent.
proposedDetectors.needs: KYC state, bonus/withdrawal events, payment tokens

proposedDetectors.rationale: Per agent-account pair, one-directional net flow, stake concentration and same-event pairing; flag extreme flow plus a shared IP/device link.
Qualify a donor at the repo constant (>= $50k lifetime house net) then require >=2 independent links to a flagged cluster; surface donor value as a review reason, never as exculpation.
Detect the base-loss -> step-up-win sequence using the repo constants (base net <= -$0.01, step-up net >= $1,000, step-up ROI >= 15%).
Per account, stake-weighted mean CLV against the closing line; flag persistent positive CLV plus high stake (sharp) separately from late-bet abuse.
Shannon entropy over sport/period/wagerType/line per account; low entropy plus high volume is a specialisation signal. Mark derived, not validated fraud evidence.
Flag bets settled unusually fast (< 30s) with >=2 corroborating signals (manual log, override, late placement).
Every finding carries source id, path, sha256, age, provenance (live-api/derived/fixture/missing), masked ids and rule version; refuse to fit or score on fixture sources.
